text.content:
Roll when you want the universe to decide. Play uses only d6s, but these creation tables use a d10 and a pair of d6s — this is character setup, not the heist. Rolled a name, Role or Flaw someone on the crew already has? Roll again, or keep it; two Faces is a choice, not a typo.

The Character Builder rolls these for you: the Roll buttons on the Species, Role, Attributes, Perks and Flaw steps, Quick Pick on the Skills step, and 2d6 for the name.

RollNameBackground
2GeraldA real spider. Has been through things. Don't ask about the incident.
3PebblesFound near the front walk. Named after the first thing they saw.
4DustyLives in the dust. One with the dust. Is, arguably, mostly dust.
5CrinkleMakes a noise when they move. Nobody knows why, least of all them.
6Jar LidWas trapped in a jar once. Has made peace with it. Jar Lid is fine.
7The ArchitectA self-given title. The crew uses it unironically because it fits.
8FilamentSilk specialist. Particular about quality. Will discuss thread count.
9NookPrefers corners. All corners. Any corner. A corner is home.
10CassetteFound in a box of old electronics. Has absorbed some energy from it.
11WidowNot a Black Widow. Just has a certain vibe. Nobody asks.
12EightSimple. Honest. Eight legs, one name. What more do you want.

RollSpecies & Vibe
1Jumping Spider — bold, visible, magnetic. Will jump at an inopportune moment.
2Orb Weaver — methodical, architectural. Strong feelings about structure.
3Wolf Spider — fast, physical, doesn't spin webs, considers this a personality.
4Cellar Spider — thin and folding, fits through anything, already inside the wall.
5Spitting Spider — precise, patient, excellent aim, almost never misses.
6Crab Spider — sideways thinker, excellent at waiting, less good at stopping.

RollRole & Summary
1The Face — you talk. To everyone. Especially the cat.
2The Ghost — you disappear. Into walls, vents, the gap behind the fridge.
3The Tinkerer — you build things out of other things. They mostly work.
4The Bruiser — you solve problems physically. Plan B is also physical.
5The Lookout — you watch, you notice, you warn the crew thirty seconds early.
6Roll again: 1–3 Wheelman (you know every exit), 4–6 Grifter (nothing is what it seems, especially you).

RollSpread (10 points)
14 · 2 · 2 · 2
23 · 3 · 2 · 2
34 · 3 · 2 · 1
43 · 3 · 3 · 1
55 · 2 · 2 · 1
64 · 4 · 1 · 1

The first number goes on the Attribute your Role's core skills use (pick one if they use two), the rest wherever you like. Add your species bonus; if that pushes anything past 5, move the extra to your lowest Attribute.

RoleBoth core skills at 3, then:
FaceStealth 3 · Perception 2 · Disguise 2 · Intimidation 2
GhostPerception 3 · Athletics 2 · Deception 2 · Engineering 2
TinkererStealth 3 · Acrobatics 2 · Tactics 2 · Athletics 2
BruiserAthletics 3 · Stealth 2 · Intimidation 2 · Perception 2
LookoutStealth 3 · Acrobatics 2 · Engineering 2 · Deception 2
WheelmanAthletics 3 · Stealth 2 · Perception 2 · Endurance 2
GrifterStealth 3 · Persuasion 2 · Perception 2 · Acrobatics 2

Perks: roll 1d6 twice on your Role's Perk table, counting down the list; reroll a repeat.

RollFlaw & Note
1Arachnophobe Magnet — humans look at you more than other spiders. A documented phenomenon.
2Overconfident — you've handled worse. (You haven't handled this.)
3Loud — not physically loud. Operationally loud. Things break near you.
4Dramatic — everything is an event. You know. You can't stop.
5Allergic to Dust — you will sneeze at the worst moment, at least once.
6Compulsive Planner — you must revise the plan, ideally right now, ideally out loud.
7Butterfingers — you will drop the thing. The important thing. At the important moment.
8Fear of Vacuums — vacuums cause immediate, total panic.
9Easily Distracted — shiny objects and interesting smells derail you.
10Show-Off — you'll take the flashier, harder approach. Sometimes it even works.

Roll when the crew starts a third round at one obstacle — the world doesn't wait — or when the night needs a nudge. Clock times in a heist (every ninety minutes, the cleaners at 8) arrive this way, or at a threshold. An entry that doesn't fit becomes its nearest equivalent: in a restaurant, the “cat” is the Rat.

RollComplicationEffect
1The cat woke up. Not because of anything the crew did. Just because.The nearest sleeping creature is active now. Nothing asleep? +1 Alert.
2A drawer slid open on its own. Something's in it. Maybe the objective. Maybe not.The ST gives the crew one detail they didn't case (never the unknown obstacle).
3A human got up for water. They're in the kitchen. Right now. Everyone freeze.Stealth +1 Difficulty here, this round and next.
4The vacuum switched on. Its cycle begins. Fear of Vacuums triggers.Its roar covers you: Stealth −1 Difficulty this round.
5A phone lit up on the counter. The room is briefly, brightly visible.No cover this round.
6Something fell off a shelf across the location. Not the crew's fault. The Alert rises by 1 anyway.That's the effect.

Roll it: [[/r 1d6]]{Mid-Heist Complication}
